{
  "title": "Why Silence Feels Louder Than Words",
  "hook_family": "recognition",
  "hook": "The silence between you feels like a door that won't open.",
  "curiosity": "Have you ever noticed how silence can speak volumes, even when it's not saying anything at all?",
  "psychological_mechanism": "Our brains are wired to fill the gaps — to imagine the worst, or the best, when words are missing.",
  "realization": "You can't hear what's left unsaid, but you feel it in your chest, like a question that never gets answered.",
  "final_line": "Sometimes, the loudest thing you can do is listen — not just to the silence, but to yourself.",
  "visual_metaphor": "A person standing at the edge of a foggy lake, watching ripples spread out from nowhere, their face half-lit by a distant, flickering lamp."
}
